title: The Fleet — overview
note: A simplified, opaque view of the fleet. The operator makes the judgment calls and wraps them in a toolkit of /fleet-* skills — the intelligent layer over the mechanical fleetc CLI — which (with the operator's own raw verbs) actuate fleetc; fleetc drives fleetd (the daemon, shown as one box — no internal state machines); fleetd actuates its external systems (a Tracker, a Forge), persists to the Ledger, works inside a Project (the worktrees), and spawns the Crew of cogs. For the real machinery (fleetd's server/scheduler/reconcile, the adapters, telemetry, flows) switch to the Full architecture.

detail.summary: Creates a git worktree + branch for a ticket (forked off the project's default branch), beside the project checkout. Pure worktree creation — no Jira lifecycle. Run when producing a dispatch, then pass the path to `fleetc dispatch --worktree`; reconcile spawns the cog there (reconcile never creates worktrees).

Launches the current branch's ship: pushes it, drafts the MR title + description from the ticket and the branch's divergence from its base, then opens the MR via `fleetc launch` (fleetd's forge adapter opens it — GitLab or GitHub alike). Run from the worktree.
Addresses the open review threads on the current branch's MR (via /mr-reply), with count-gating and outcome propagation so the sailor knows what was resolved.

Rebases the current branch's MR against its target. Clean divergence → triggers GitLab's server-side rebase via `fleetc rebase` and exits (the sailor re-fires on the result). Conflict → resolves locally with project/code understanding and force-pushes. Escalates only when the conflict needs a product/design decision.
Classifies a broken GitLab pipeline on the current branch and attempts a good-faith fix (retry / lint / build / test / infra); escalates if it's unclassifiable or out of scope.

The operator's "pawn it off" handoff: yields a hand's work to a sailor. Reports `concluded` via fleetc, so fleetd promotes the order to auto, moves Jira → In QA, requests review, and reaps the hand. A ticketless hand has no sailor to yield to. Run from the hand's worktree.

detail.type: skill · ship the viewer to Splash
detail.summary: Builds the demos/architecture viewer into a single self-contained HTML file and publishes it to a Splash page at a stable, SSO-gated URL (Okta handled via a vendored Chrome extension — no token or persisted cookie). First run creates the page and returns its URL; later runs replace the same page.
On the Overview fleetd is one opaque box. Inside, its heart is a single scheduling loop (scheduler.rs::run) — the state machine below — that the full view hides.

stateMachine.note: Verified against scheduler.rs::run. Each pass fires any ticker whose Instant deadline has passed, then blocks on the mpsc command channel for ≤500ms (Timeout → re-loop). poll is READ-ONLY (overwrites the in-memory liveness snapshot — no ledger write, no event); sync, live reconcile, and each client command are the single writer's writes — one transaction appending a CDC event. A Disconnected channel (UDS server gone) breaks the loop. Cadences shown are the config defaults (5/300/60s), re-read live each pass.
